tasks.title: Stage 1. MVP
tasks.statement: The short-video service launches with 250 reads and 30 metadata writes per second. Build the simplest design — users, an app server, a database — and pick sizes so that load stays at or below 80% and the cost is $250 per month.
tasks.hint: An S server handles 300 requests (280 is 93%), so you need an M. An S database is enough: 250 reads and 30 writes is 40%.

tasks.title: Stage 2. Tenfold growth
tasks.statement: Load has grown to 2,500 reads and 300 writes per second, with a 5 GB working set. Strengthen the design: a load balancer, several servers, a metadata cache (≥85%) and a database replica with automatic failover. The design survives a database, cache and server failure, load is at most 80%, and the budget is $1,400 per month.
tasks.hint: Five M servers; a 5 GB cache with TTL 3600 and a replica; an M database (300 writes is too much for an S) with a replica and automatic failover.

tasks.title: Stage 3. Video and CDN
tasks.statement: Users have started watching videos: 30,000 file requests per second. Move the files to object storage and put a CDN (≥90% of static requests) in front of it. The app servers must stay on metadata only, load at most 80%, the design stays resilient, and the budget is $1,500 per month.
tasks.hint: CDN → storage (static traffic bypasses the servers); the CDN passes dynamic requests to the load balancer. Everything else is as in stage 2.

tasks.title: Stage 4. Transcoding through a queue
tasks.statement: Videos must be transcoded after upload. Add a queue and idempotent workers on spot instances (at least two): after a 10-second peak the queue drains with no lag (5 s is acceptable), the database and servers stay at or below 80%, and the budget is $1,600 per month.
tasks.hint: Server → queue → workers → database. Two M workers handle 800 writes per second at a load of 300.

tasks.title: Stage 5. Feed and search
tasks.statement: A subscription feed (100 followers per author on average) and title search (15% of reads, a 160 GB index) have been added. Choose the hybrid feed, add a search cluster (shards by volume, two replicas) and expand the cache to the working set (8 GB, ≥85%). The design survives a database and search failure, everything stays at or below 80%, and the budget is $3,500 per month.
tasks.hint: Feed — set the server to “hybrid”. Search: four shards, two replicas (160 / 40 = 4). An 8 GB cache with a replica. The hybrid feed doubles writes, so an M database is already tight — you need an L.

tasks.title: Stage 6. Zones and protection
tasks.statement: The service has become critical: it must survive a zone, a deployment and a server failure. Spread the servers, cache, workers and database across three zones, enable a rolling deployment and a circuit breaker, put a rate limiter at the entry (limit at least the normal load of 2,800) and add monitoring. Load at most 80%, budget $4,200 per month.
tasks.hint: Nine M servers across three zones (after losing a zone, six remain — 4,200). Put the rate limiter between the load balancer and the servers; add monitoring to the design.

tasks.title: Stage 7. Cut the bill
tasks.statement: The bill keeps growing while load is stable: the app servers are needed around the clock. Move them to the reserved pricing plan (a discount of about 40%) while keeping all the reliability goals: the design survives a zone, deployment, server, database and search failure, load is at most 80%, and the budget is $3,700 per month.
tasks.hint: The app server's “Pricing” parameter — “reserved”. Leave everything else alone: reliability matters more than saving on it.

tasks.title: Exam. The final design
tasks.statement: Final assignment. The service at full strength: 45,000 file requests per second, 3,800 reads and 450 writes per second, a subscription feed (100 followers per author), search (15% of reads, a 240 GB index), a 10 GB working set. Build the design from scratch: CDN (≥90%) → storage; load balancers (two), a rate limiter (limit from 4,300), servers with a rolling deployment, a circuit breaker and a hybrid feed; a cache (≥85%) with a replica; a queue with idempotent workers on spot instances; search (shards by volume, two replicas); a database with a replica and automatic failover; monitoring. The design survives a zone, deployment, server, database, cache and search failure; availability ≥ 99.9%, p99 ≤ 160 ms, load at most 80%, budget $4,700 per month.
tasks.hint: Eleven M servers across three zones, reserved pricing; a 10 GB cache with a replica in three zones; search with 6 shards × 2 replicas; three M workers on spot instances; an L database with a replica in three zones; everything else as in the stages of the previous exercises.
